prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

S722: Each isolation device is secured against unintended operation using the site-approved locking and tagging method.
S723: Personal protection is applied in accordance with the permit and local electrical safety rules.
S724: Electrical absence-of-voltage checks are performed at the work location using suitable, tested equipment.
S725: Stored energy, induced voltage, and other hazardous energy sources are assessed before hands-on work begins.
S726: The Field Supervisor confirms that every crew member understands the limits of the approved work area.
S727: Changes to the task, equipment state, or work location require a review of the boundary before work continues.
S728: The Work Permit Portal retains the current approval and makes superseded versions unavailable for active work.
S729: Control room staff and the field team use the same revision when confirming isolation status.
S730: A shift handover records outstanding isolations, affected equipment, and any restrictions that remain in force.
S731: The incoming team independently checks the boundary status before accepting responsibility for ongoing work.
S732: No isolation is removed until the work is complete, personnel and tools are accounted for, and the responsible authority approves restoration.
S733: The person removing each control confirms that the associated work party is clear of the hazard area.
S734: The Control Engineer verifies the restoration state and communicates any remaining operational limitation to affected personnel.
S735: Boundary records are closed only after the equipment state has been confirmed and the permit has been updated.
S736: Substation switching windows are coordinated with planned maintenance so that equipment is available only when the required operating conditions can be maintained.
S737: The Duty Planner consolidates proposed work periods and identifies tasks that require a change to substation configuration.
S738: The Maintenance Planning Engine checks task durations, dependencies, and resource assumptions before a window is proposed.
S739: The Grid Dispatcher confirms that the requested period is compatible with export requirements and network operating limits.
S740: The approved window includes a start time, an end time, the affected equipment, and the expected operating state.
S741: The Substation Operator reviews the switching sequence and confirms that each step can be performed within the available interval.
S742: The Control Engineer checks that turbine operations can be managed safely while the substation work is in progress.
S743: The Grid Interface Relay remains available for the required protection and control functions throughout the planned work.
S744: Work on the Main Transformer is scheduled only after its expected loading and required isolation duration have been reviewed.
